reason:
Split verdict, as instructed. THE TWO DEAD BUTTONS: real, verified in source and by driving. render-b.js:681 builds act("Send the link", true) and act("Copy the link") with no attrs, so neither carries data-act; the only delegated click listener lives in wireOwner (render-b.js:499) and states.publish never calls it. Driven at 1440, 1280, 768 and 390: publish holds exactly two .b-act buttons, both data-act=null; clicking each leaves document.body.innerHTML byte-identical with zero console output, and the state renders zero [role=status] or [aria-live] nodes, so nothing is announced either. The gate claim is exact too: the dead-control loop at interaction-check.mjs:539 iterates ['owner-flight','owner-empty'] only and scopes to .b-field button, so publish is the one state it never visits. It breaks the lab's own rule stated at render-b.js:255 ("Anything not built is inert text, never a focusable promise"), on the screen b.css:534 calls the ceremony. This half is real and lands on the same defect another seat's confirmed verdict (the-ceremony-has-two-ornamental-buttons-and-no-way-back) reached independently, so the panel should merge them, not double-count them.

THE UNFURL PROMOTION: refuted, and factually wrong about what is on screen. The card is not a caption sitting inert in a left column: states.publish (render-b.js:667-671) already gives it the whole first column under its own label "What lands in the message", and card() is a real <a href=https://timeline.signalstudio.ie/s/... aria-label="Mara and Finn, a wedding timeline">, not an inert div. At 1440 the grid is 320px + 684px (b.css:734) and the card measures 300x218 at the top of the left column. Moving it into the right column "at the same width as the message block" would set it at 684px, breaking the deliberate max-width:300px at b.css:590-597 whose preceding comment records this card being repaired once already. The card's whole job is to show, at true size, the object that lands in a message thread; blown to 684px it stops being a preview and becomes a hero banner, which makes the sentence directly beside it ("This is what lands in the message") false. That is trading a working truth for a bigger picture, on the screen whose CSS comment already says the ceremony IS the card held up. The supporting measurement is also loose: content ends at y499 of 960 at 1440 and 1280, so the empty band is 48%, not "roughly 55%", and at 768 and 390 the state fills 726px and 714px of 960.
sharpenedFix: Fix only the controls; leave the card where it is at 300px. (1) Give Copy the link data-act="copy" and make it the primary; write F.shareUrlFull (the https URL, not the display-trimmed F.shareUrl) with navigator.clipboard.writeText, flip the label to "Copied" for 2s and restore it. (2) There is no live region to reuse - publish renders none - so add an empty [role=status] beside .b-note inside states.publish and write "Link copied." into it on success, and "Copy did not work. Select the link and copy it by hand." on the rejection path, rather than failing silently. (3) Do not put navigator.share behind Send the link: publish is a `full` medium (MEDIUM map, render-b.js:781) driven in desktop Chromium where navigator.share does not exist, so it would be a second dead button wearing a handler; a mailto: is likewise a promise the lab cannot keep. Demote it to inert("Send the link") - the helper and .b-inert already exist and are used in owner-empty - and let the one working Copy carry the screen. Deleting BOTH buttons, the finding's stated alternative, is the wrong branch: a share screen with no copy control is worse than the defect. (4) states.publish must call wireOwner (or a minimal wire) for any of this - today it is unwired - and the handler needs a `copy` branch. (5) Close the class rather than this instance: run the dead-control loop at interaction-check.mjs:539 over every state in the config instead of the hand-listed two, and add one assertion that pressing Copy the link changes its label and writes the [role=status] line.
